name: Keratinocyte (skin cell)
short_description: Polyhedral epidermal cell joined to its neighbours by desmosomal "spines", packed with keratin tonofilament bundles; differentiates upward from the basal layer, produces keratohyalin and lamellar bodies, and finally cornifies into the anucleate, waterproof outer skin barrier.

textbook.1: PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — polyhedral (not round) cell studded with spiky desmosomal projections at the vertices, large central nucleus with chromatin texture, keratin tonofilament bundles converging on desmosomes, irregular clumped keratohyalin granules, ovoid lamellar bodies with internal lipid striping, dark crescent melanosome cap above the nucleus, rough ER, Golgi, mitochondria; matches house palette/line style, no border, no text.

sem.1: PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — polyhedral cell with domed nuclear bulge, surface studded with short blunt desmosomal spikes giving the classic prickle-cell texture, coral-pink false colour on dark charcoal background, shallow depth of field, surface-only (no interior drawn), single specimen, no border/text.

3d.1: PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — polyhedral cell with spiky desmosomal projections, natural warm biological tones, translucent nucleus, dark clumped keratohyalin granules, crescent melanosome cap, striped mitochondria, rough ER, Golgi, subsurface scattering on membrane; no border, no text.

watercolor.1: PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — aged paper fills the full frame edge-to-edge (no separate sheet/mat/border), polyhedral prickle-cell silhouette with spiky desmosomal outline, ink-lined interior showing nucleus, keratohyalin clumps, lamellar bodies, melanosome cap wash, rough ER, Golgi, mitochondria; single specimen, no text.

reference: PASS — Wikimedia Commons "Micrograph of keratinocytes, basal cells and melanocytes in the epidermis.jpg" (CC BY 4.0, Setijanti et al., Alternatives to Animal Testing, Springer 2019). Genuine H&E light photomicrograph of human epidermis with pointer-arrow labels confirming keratinocyte/basal-cell/melanocyte identity; cleaned text-free version (edit_image.py) preserves the original purple/pink H&E colorization and is used for display.
